content.title: Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin: How to watch tonight, full fight card, streaming info and more
content.text: Alycia Baumgardner will face Bo Mi Re Shin this weekend in an all-women's boxing event at Madison Square Garden, here's how to watch. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) (Sarah Stier via Getty Images)A multi-year agreement between Most Valuable Promotions and ESPN has guaranteed that ESPN will be the official broadcast partner of MVP women's boxing events through 2028, and one of the first fights to air as part of that deal is this Friday's match between Alycia Baumgartner and Bo Mi Re Shin. The super featherweight title bout will take place at Madison Square Garden, and will be co-headlined by a super middleweight title defense between reigning champ Shadasia Green and Lani Daniels.The fight takes place on Friday, April 17. Prelim coverage begins at 6:30 p.m. ET, with main ringwalks set for approximately 10 p.m. The main card will be available on ESPN and ESPN Unlimited, and prelims will stream exclusively on ESPN+. Here's everything you need to know about the Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin fight and the entire fight card.AdvertisementDate: Friday, April 17Start time: Prelim coverage begins around 6:30 p.m. ET / 3:30 p.m. PTMain Ringwalks: 10 p.m. ET / 7 p.m. PTLocation: Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, New York CityTV channel: ESPNStreaming: ESPN Unlimited, Fubo, Sling, DirecTV and more, prelims on ESPN+When is the Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin fight?The Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin fight is this Friday, April 17. The broadcast begins at 10 p.m. ET. Prelims will stream at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+.What channel is the Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin fight on?The Baumgardner vs. Shin fight and all other bouts on the main fight card will air on ESPN. Prelims will air on ESPN+, which you can find on the ESPN app with a subscription to either ESPN Unlimited or ESPN Select.AdvertisementWhere to watch Alycia Baumgardner vs. Bo Mi Re Shin:ESPN's streaming platform offers thousands of exclusive live events, original studio shows and acclaimed series that air across ESPN's suite of seven linear channels, as well as exclusive content on ESPN+, ABC on ESPN, SEC+, ACCNX and more. The new tier costs $29.99/month or $299.99/year. ESPN Select allows subscribers to access exclusive content only available on the app, and an extensive archive of on-demand content (including the entire 30 For 30 library, select ESPN Films, game replays and more). Whether you purchase a standalone plan, add-on or Disney bundle plan, the service provides access to thousands of sports events for $12.99/month or $129.99/year. Sling TV's Day Pass gives consumers the freedom to watch what they want, when they want, without committing to a monthly streaming subscription. Sign up for a single day ($4.99), a weekend ($9.99), or a full week ($14.99) and watch every channel available through Sling Orange, which includes ESPN and ESPN2, and over 30 more channels. No strings attached. Day Pass is ideal if you want to catch a specific event like Friday night's fight card without subscribing to a monthly streaming plan. Main Card (ESPN)Alycia Baumgardner (17-1, 7 KOs) vs. Bo Mi Re Shin (19-3-3, 10 KOs) — 10 rounds, super featherweight, unified WBA/IBF/WBO title fightShadasia Green (16-1, 11 KOs) vs. Lani Daniels (11-4-2, 1 KO) — 10 rounds, super middleweight, world title defenseTamm Thibeault (4-0, 3 KOs) vs. Nadja Jesus (5-0, 3 KOs) — 10 rounds, middleweightKrystal Rosado (8-1, 2 KOs) vs. Fernanda Reyes (8-0) — 8 rounds, bantamweightPreliminary Card (ESPN+, ESPN App)Jahmal Harvey (2-0) vs. Leandro Medina (7-3-1) — lightweightJavon "Wanna" Walton (3-0-1) vs. Dionne Ruvalcaba (2-2) — lightweightRaquel Miller (13-0) vs. Adriana Araujo (6-3) — super middleweightNat Dove (7-0-1) vs. Maria Micheo (14-6) — flyweightElon De Jesus (11-1-2) vs. Connor Adaway (10-2-1) — super bantamweightAlex Vargas (14-0) vs. Ryan O'Rourke (13-0)
